subject: Social Habits
title: Saying sorry and forgiving
objectives: Children will say sorry when they have hurt someone, with support.
Children will say "it is okay" and help to make things better.
content: Saying sorry, saying "it is okay", and making things better.
teachingActivities: Never force an empty sorry; first help the child notice the hurt ("Ada is crying, she is sad"); model sorry and make-it-better actions; teach the friend to say "it is okay" only if they feel it; keep it brief and kind; no shaming or time-out for toddlers.
learnerActivities: Say sorry with support and help a friend who is upset.
resources: Pictures of hurt and sorry scenes
A plaster toy and a soft toy
assessment: Observe whether each child says sorry with a prompt and helps a friend who is upset.
expectedOutcomes: Helps a friend who is upset.

lessons.title: Saying sorry
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will say sorry when they have hurt someone, with support.
successCriteria: Looks at the friend who was hurt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, follow instructions and play with friends.
resources: A picture of a hurt friend
lessons.starter: Show one puppet bumping another and say "Oh no! The puppet is sad. We say sorry."
teacherActivities: Show the puppet saying sorry in a kind voice.
Say "Sorry means I did not want to hurt you."
Practise saying sorry to a puppet.
learnerActivities: Child says sorry to the puppet.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the puppet saying sorry in a kind voice. Children: Children watch and say sorry.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Sorry means I did not want to hurt you." Children: Children repeat sorry.
Step 3. Teacher: Practise saying sorry to a puppet. Children: Child says sorry to the puppet.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Thank you for saying sorry." Children: Children smile.

practical.title: Puppet sorry
practical.safety: Keep puppet play gentle and never use a real child as the example. Never force sorry; help the child notice how the friend feels.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say why we say sorry.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say when we hurt someone?

expectedOutcomes: Looks at the friend who was hurt
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say sorry to the puppet.
lessons.homeConnection: Help your child notice another person’s feelings before saying sorry.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say sorry when they have hurt someone, with support" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Sorry, sorry, I am sorry. Let me help you feel better.

lessons.title: It is okay
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will say "it is okay" when a friend says sorry.
successCriteria: Says it is okay with a prompt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, follow instructions and play with friends.
resources: A picture of friends making up
lessons.starter: Let one puppet say sorry and the other say "It is okay. Let us play."
teacherActivities: Show how the second puppet says it is okay.
Practise in pairs: one says sorry, one says it is okay.
Swap roles so everyone has a go.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say it is okay.
Child says sorry or it is okay.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how the second puppet says it is okay. Children: Children watch and say it is okay.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "We forgive our friends." Children: Children repeat forgive with support.
Step 3. Teacher: Practise in pairs: one says sorry, one says it is okay. Children: Child says sorry or it is okay.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap roles so everyone has a go. Children: Child swaps and practises again.

practical.title: Sorry and okay
practical.safety: Keep the practice make-believe with puppets or dolls and supervise closely. Never ask a hurt child to forgive before they are ready.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say another way to make up.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we say after sorry?

expectedOutcomes: Says it is okay with a prompt
lessons.conclusion: Shake hands or wave and say friends.
lessons.homeConnection: Say "it is okay" when your child says sorry and show forgiveness.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say "it is okay" when a friend says sorry" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Making it better
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will do something kind to help a friend who is upset.
successCriteria: Gets an adult when a friend is hurt
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, follow instructions and play with friends.
lessons.starter: Show a sad soft toy and say "How can we make it feel better?"
teacherActivities: Show ways to help: a smile, a tissue, a toy or getting the teacher.
Let children comfort the soft toy.
Say "If a friend is hurt, get the teacher."
Practise running to the teacher at a walk.
learnerActivities: Children look and choose a way.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show ways to help: a smile, a tissue, a toy or getting the teacher. Children: Children look and choose a way.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children comfort the soft toy. Children: Child comforts the toy gently.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "If a friend is hurt, get the teacher." Children: Children repeat get the teacher.
Step 4. Teacher: Practise running to the teacher at a walk. Children: Child walks to the teacher.

practical.title: Help a friend
practical.safety: Keep play gentle and the floor clear. Never encourage children to treat real injuries; always get an adult.

differentiation.support: Choose a way to help together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to think of a way to help a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How can we help a friend?

lessons.conclusion: Hug the soft toy and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Show your child how to comfort someone who is upset.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "do something kind to help a friend who is upset" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sorry story
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will act out a short story where sorry and forgiving put things right.
successCriteria: Uses sorry or it is okay in role play
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, follow instructions and play with friends.
lessons.starter: Tell a short story: "Two friends built a tower. One knocked it down by mistake. What happened next?"
teacherActivities: Tell the story slowly with pictures and puppets.
Act out saying sorry and building again together.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell the story slowly with pictures and puppets. Children: Children listen and look.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "How did the friend feel?" Children: Child says sad.
Step 3. Teacher: Act out saying sorry and building again together. Children: Child acts out the story.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "They made things better." Children: Children say better.

practical.title: Tower story
practical.safety: Use large light blocks and supervise falling towers. Keep the story gentle and the ending kind.

differentiation.support: Act the story with the child and help with words.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell the story to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Uses sorry and it is okay in role play
lessons.homeConnection: Tell a short sorry story at bedtime.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "act out a short story where sorry and forgiving put things right" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 4 sorry check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child says sorry and helps a friend.
successCriteria: Helps a friend who is upset
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can listen, follow instructions and play with friends.
lessons.starter: Sing the sorry song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: sorry, it is okay and make it better.
At each station watch how the child responds.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: sorry, it is okay and make it better. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child responds. Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Sorry stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep play gentle. Use puppets and soft toys only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to explain sorry to a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says sorry; says it is okay; helps a friend who is upset; gets an adult when needed.

questions.question: What do we say when we hurt someone?
What do we say after sorry?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
Says sorry and helps with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep modelling sorry and forgiving at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child says sorry and helps a friend" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
